Both drivers and bus crews were arr
item.content:encoded:
Police in Enga arrested 32 people for various summary offences as part of a major Independence law enforcement blitz across the province.

Acting Provincial Police Commander [PPC] Chief Inspector Daniel Yangen confirmed the arrests, which target reckless road behaviour, illegal gambling, public drunkenness, and drinking inside moving Public Motor Vehicles [PMVs]. Both drivers and bus crews were arrested for allowing passengers to consume alcohol on board.

Chief Inspector Yangen admitted that many of these summary offences had become normalised over the years due to lax law enforcement by police.

However, he assured the public that despite manpower shortages, he will strictly enforce the law at all levels during his tenure as Acting PPC and Wabag Police Station Commander.

In a direct warning to his own family and community members, Chief Inspector Yangen cautioned against relying on traditional ties to avoid prosecution. He warned that relatives attempting to use the wantok system for leniency would be charged with obstructing police duties.

Police have also announced strict bail conditions to deter offenders during the 51st Independence anniversary celebrations including; unlicensed sale of alcohol – K5,000 bail; public alcohol consumption and homebrew offences – K1,000 bail; illegal gambling including Bingo and card games – K1,000 bail; fighting in public places – K1,000 bail; and, cultivating, selling, or possessing marijuana – No bail.

While urging the public to celebrate the nation’s 51st Independence anniversary peacefully and responsibly, Chief Inspector Yangen stressed that police will maintain zero tolerance for lawlessness across Enga Province.

item.title: PA Kaiyun outlines roadmap for Western
item.description: Western province now has a clear blueprint for sustainable growth following the completion of its Provincial Integrated Plan, says Provincial Administrator Robert Alphonse Kaiyun. item.content:encoded:
Western province now has a clear blueprint for sustainable growth following the completion of its Provincial Integrated Plan, says Provincial Administrator Robert Alphonse Kaiyun.

Delivering his 51st Independence Anniversary message in Daru today, Mr Kaiyun highlighted that Western is among the first provinces in the country to finalise its Integrated Development Plan [2023–2027], alongside individual district plans for South, Delta, Middle, and North Fly.

He said the provincial administration is now shifting focus to completing Ward and Local Level Government [LLG] plans to eliminate adhoc development projects.

Emphasising human capital as the key driver of long-term change, Kaiyun pointed to major infrastructure investments, including new dormitories completed at Kiunga Secondary School in 2025 to boost student retention for Grade 12s.

He acknowledged ongoing support from key development partners, including the Sustainable Development Program [SDP], Ok Tedi Mining Limited [OTML], Ok Tedi Development Foundation [OTDF[, local churches, and the National Government in advancing education, healthcare, and road connectivity.

Over the next 12 months, the provincial administration will focus on eight priority areas including; response to El Niño dry weather disaster, grand opening of the new Fly River Provincial Government Assembly House, advancement of the Daru Uplift Program, including the new Daru Urban LLG office, relocation of South Fly District headquarters to Wipim, empowerment of LLGs for improved local governance, implementation of the 1-6-6 education structure, healthcare improvements in partnership with the Western Provincial Health Authority, and, targeted investments in agriculture, livestock, fisheries, climate change, and biodiversity conservation.

On public sector governance, Mr Kaiyun reminded civil servants of their statutory duty of accountability under Section 119 of the Organic Law, urging them to serve the people with integrity.

He also called on unemployed residents living in Daru town to return to their home villages and participate in productive land use.

The PA concluded by calling on leaders, youth, and communities across the province to unite around a 'reset agenda' to help build a stronger nation.

item.title: Forgotten by distance, not by patriotism
item.description: They may be far from the centres of power, but the people of Green River have once again shown that distance cannot diminish their love for Papua New Guinea. Communities from Abaru, Green River Station and Deo gathered at Green River Station to mark the country’s 51st Independence Anniversary, turning a last-minute celebration into a strong display of community spirit and national pride.
item.content:encoded:
They may be far from the centres of power, but the people of Green River have once again shown that distance cannot diminish their love for Papua New Guinea.

Communities from Abaru, Green River Station and Deo gathered at Green River Station to mark the country’s 51st Independence Anniversary, turning a last-minute celebration into a strong display of community spirit and national pride.

The celebrations came together despite delays in funding, which left little time for communities to prepare for the national occasion.

Ward 18 Commissioner for Abaru Green River Station, Koms Mangofia, said he was delighted to see the people still come together to celebrate their country despite the challenges.

The District provided K5,000 for every wards to celebrate the Independence , so Abaru and Deo put together their money, making it K10,000 for them to celebrate in a meaningful way. For Mangofia, the gathering was also an opportunity to remember the late Grand Chief Sir Michael Somare, whose leadership helped shape the nation that today brings together hundreds of communities, cultures and languages under one flag.

He said the people of Green River may live in a remote part of PNG, but their commitment to the country remains strong.

The celebrations have already brought communities together through volleyball and basketball, with children’s sprinting and other traditional and fun activities to continue through Saturday.

But behind the celebrations is a broader appeal.

Mangofia is calling on provincial, district and LLG authorities to make Independence funding available on time, saying this would allow remote communities to organise celebrations on a larger and more meaningful scale.

Green River is one of the communities far removed from PNG’s major urban centres, where access to government services and development opportunities can be challenging.

Yet, when Independence Day arrives, the people still gather.

With limited resources, little preparation time and the challenges of remoteness, they have chosen not to let those circumstances silence their national pride.

Their message from the far reaches of West Sepik is simple: PNG belongs to every community — not only those closest to the centres of government.

The Green River celebrations will continue until Saturday.

Mangofia has extended his Independence greetings to the people of Green River, West Sepik and Papua New Guinea, wishing all citizens a Happy 51st Independence Anniversary.

item.title: ‘Independence demands action’: Basil
item.description: Bulolo MP Sam Basil Jr says Papua New Guinea’s 51st Independence anniversary should be a time for citizens to reflect on what they are doing to improve their communities and the country. In his Independence message, Basil said Independence was not only about celebrating freedom but also about taking responsibility for the future.
item.content:encoded:
Bulolo MP Sam Basil Jr says Papua New Guinea’s 51st Independence anniversary should be a time for citizens to reflect on what they are doing to improve their communities and the country.

In his Independence message, Basil said Independence was not only about celebrating freedom but also about taking responsibility for the future.

“It is our individual contribution and what we do every day that contributes to our common good and determines our value as the people of Bulolo and PNG,” Basil said.

He said Bulolo had changed significantly since independence, but many of the district’s development challenges remained. Basil pointed to the condition of roads, limited access to services, employment opportunities, law and order, education and the need to strengthen agriculture and other income-generating activities.

He also reflected on Bulolo’s history, noting that the district once had a busy airstrip, theatres, libraries, stores and other services during its mining and forestry development. He said the challenge now was for Papua New Guineans to build on that history and create communities that could meet today’s needs.

Basil said his focus in Bulolo included health supplies, support for schools, food and cash crops, which he described as investments in social and economic empowerment.

“These are small activities and programs and we may not see the results now or in five years,” he said. “But if we continue and our people become strong and healthy, respect the law and ensure order, we can have strong independent communities with improved living standards.”

Basil also called on leaders at political, government, business, church and community levels to have a clear vision and make a difference in the lives of the people they serve. He said citizens also had a responsibility to respect other people, their property and privacy to maintain safe and secure communities.

“Every leader at every level of leadership ... must have a vision of how we want to make a difference in the lives of the people which we lead,” he said.

Basil thanked past and present political leaders, churches, businesses and communities for their contribution to Bulolo’s development. He said the district’s future would depend on the combined efforts of its people.

“We will continue to celebrate our Independence and our destiny, if we also continue to contribute our bit,” he said.

item.title: Rosso asks what comes next
item.description: Papua New Guinea must now look beyond its first 51 years of independence and decide what it wants for the generations ahead, Deputy Prime Minister John Rosso says. Rosso, who is also the Lae MP, was the principal guest at Lae’s 51st Independence anniversary celebration at Sir Ignatius Kilage Stadium on Wednesday.
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea must now look beyond its first 51 years of independence and decide what it wants for the generations ahead, Deputy Prime Minister John Rosso says.

Rosso, who is also the Lae MP, was the principal guest at Lae’s 51st Independence anniversary celebration at Sir Ignatius Kilage Stadium on Wednesday.

In his speech, Rosso reflected on 16 September 1975 and his memories of watching the Australian flag come down and the Papua New Guinean flag rise.

He paid tribute to the leaders who guided the country to independence, including Grand Chief Sir Michael Somare and Sir Julius Chan.

Rosso said Papua New Guinea had achieved independence peacefully despite its many languages, cultures and communities.

He said that unity remained important as the country entered its next 50 years.

“What do we want for the next 50 years?” Rosso asked.

He said Independence Day should be more than a celebration. It should also be a time for Papua New Guineans to think about the country they want to leave for their children and grandchildren.

Rosso also remembered former Lae MP and Morobe leader Songar Luthawake, whose first anniversary of death falls this week.

He urged Papua New Guineans to remember the sacrifices of earlier generations while taking responsibility for the country’s future.

item.title: West Sepik challenged to reset as PNG celebrates 51st Independence
item.description: As Papua New Guinea celebrates its 51st Independence Anniversary, West Sepik Province has been challenged to reset and refocus for the next 50 years. The call was made by West Sepik Provincial Administrator, Jacob Areman, during the 51st Independence flag-raising ceremony at Pope Francis Oval in Vanimo.
item.content:encoded:
As Papua New Guinea celebrates its 51st Independence Anniversary, West Sepik Province has been challenged to reset and refocus for the next 50 years.

The call was made by West Sepik Provincial Administrator, Jacob Areman, during the 51st Independence flag-raising ceremony at Pope Francis Oval in Vanimo.

The ceremony was officiated by members of the three disciplinary forces - the Royal PNG Constabulary, PNG Defence Force and Correctional Service.

Mr. Areman delivered his address under the provincial theme: "Sharing Our Vision, Admitting Our Challenges and Resetting for Our Future."

He said West Sepik has shared the same vision with the rest of the country and has contributed significantly to national development over the past 50 years.

He said the province has produced human resource leaders, bureaucrats, foreign service officers, medical professionals and contributed to economic growth through the forestry sector.

However, the Provincial Administrator admitted that despite these contributions, the province itself continues to struggle.

"Though West Sepik has contributed well to the country's development, the province itself has been struggling with major infrastructure developments such as poor road conditions, water and sanitation, electricity, health and education," he said.

He added that with no major cash crops or industries to generate internal revenue, the province depends entirely on National Government grants, which often affects service delivery.

"These have been the province's and the country's major challenges in the last 51 years. For West Sepik, though we face these challenges, we have come a long way."

Mr. Areman said it is now time for West Sepik to reset, refocus and rebuild for the next 50 years.

He reminded the people that the province's long-term vision is to transform Vanimo into a City, Aitape into an Industrial Hub, and the Vanimo-Green Corridor into a Free Trade Zone for both West Sepik and Papua New Guinea.

He urged all citizens, including elites and leaders of West Sepik, to work together and focus on developing the province.

item.description: As Papua New Guinea marks its 51 years of Indepdence a lesson in traditional Chinese culture has offered international journalists in Bejing China a different perspective on the role of language, broadcasting, and journalism in preserving knowledge and cultural identity. As part of their training in China, the journalists were introduced to the ancient practice of rubbing, used to reproduce inscri
item.content:encoded:
As Papua New Guinea marks its 51 years of Indepdence a lesson in traditional Chinese culture has offered international journalists in Bejing China a different perspective on the role of language, broadcasting, and journalism in preserving knowledge and cultural identity.

As part of their training in China, the journalists were introduced to the ancient practice of rubbing, used to reproduce inscriptions and passed down texts before modern printing became widespread.

That lesson unexpectedly connects to Papua New Guinea's own experience. Since independence, broadcasting in local languages has helped communities access information in familiar, meaningful ways.

The National Broadcasting Corporation of Papua New Guinea has continued that role. From radio to establishing of local language TV news early this year 2026, preserving language through modern journalism.

While tools change, the goal remains, carrying stories forward, so future generations can hear them.

item.title: Pokanis hails 51 years of bilateral ties with Philippines
item.description: Papua New Guinea’s Ambassador to the Philippines, Stephen Pokanis, has extended warm independence greetings to both nations while celebrating 51 years of strong bilateral relations and economic partnership. Speaking on the country’s 51st Independence Anniversary, Pokanis acknowledged the Government and people of the Republic of the Philippines as the first international community to formally recog
item.content:encoded:
Papua New Guinea’s Ambassador to the Philippines, Stephen Pokanis, has extended warm independence greetings to both nations while celebrating 51 years of strong bilateral relations and economic partnership.

Speaking on the country’s 51st Independence Anniversary, Pokanis acknowledged the Government and people of the Republic of the Philippines as the first international community to formally recognise PNG’s independence on Sept 16, 1975 .

"Since then, our two governments have established diplomatic and economic ties coinciding with the Trade and Investment Partnership Agreement and established a Joint Economic and Trade Committee to boost cooperation," Pokanis said .

He said key areas of ongoing collaboration include agriculture, fisheries technology transfer, aquaculture, manufacturing, and air services.

Current trade between the two countries sees PNG exporting major commodities such as copper ore and frozen fish, while importing processed goods and food items from the Philippines .

Pokanis said the growing people-to-people connections, has paved way for more than 38,000 Filipinos who currently reside and work in Papua New Guinea, forming the nation's largest international community.

"Filipino professionals are contributing expansively to Papua New Guinea’s healthcare, education, business, mining, gas and oil industries, and infrastructure development," he said .

He expressed confidence in the continuing growth of the relationship, praying for ongoing prosperity and successful friendship between both countries .

item.title: 17 escape in Goroka cell breach
item.description: Seventeen prisoners escaped from the Goroka Police Station cell lockup on Monday night while officers were finalising security plans for major upcoming events.

item.description: As Papua New Guinea celebrates its 51st Independence, inmates at the Bundaira Correctional Institution in Kainantu, Eastern Highlands, will also mark the occasion and take time to reflect on their lives.
